component.name: MASCHERA
component.summary: Mask personal data in documents, entirely offline

description.p: MASCHERA finds and replaces personal data in documents — names, addresses, dates of birth, social security and case numbers — so a text can be shown, shared or given to an online service without handing over the people in it.

Everything happens on the machine. The document is not uploaded, and there is no endpoint that could send it anywhere. The model runs locally; the only time MASCHERA uses the network is the one download of that model on first start, and it asks before doing so.
Built for Swiss documents, in the three official languages of the Confederation — German, French and Italian — as well as English. Rumantsch is not supported.

This is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation: the replacements are kept in a dictionary, so a masked text can be turned back. That is a feature for reviewing a case, and a responsibility for storing the dictionary.

description.p: Clearer wording: messages when fetching the model on first start, console output at start-up and several error messages read more plainly.

A new look, designed together with a UX architect. The window reads as six cards along the way from original to final text, with a step bar on top that follows your progress and jumps to a card on click. Green marks what stays on your device, orange what leaves it. New typefaces (IBM Plex Sans and Mono), new colours in light and dark. Values kept in plain text on purpose now carry a light grey frame. The vocabulary can be filtered by group. The notice about remaining placeholders can be closed. Fewer settings: one typeface option and the switch for buttons and labels are gone.

The first release with feedback from testers. Settings have a footer with Cancel and Save; Escape and a click beside the dialog cancel. An error when saving appears next to the section it belongs to. The logo reads well on dark backgrounds, and the program icon has a thin light edge. Screenshots for software stores. Security: the Docker image no longer ships pip.

Remove a mask from the vocabulary with one click, everywhere in the document. "Check for updates" in the menu. Clearer separators when the window is narrow. Security hardening: the model is fetched from a fixed commit, uploaded file names never become paths, and a loud warning when host checking is switched off.

Security update: Werkzeug 3.1.9 (a request could hang the Windows version) and the newest Python 3.13 in every build. Dropping something that is not a file, such as a message straight from Apple Mail, now explains what to do instead of doing nothing.

The button that copies the prompt and opens the AI service now opens it like a menu link on macOS and Windows. The list of services is alphabetical and includes Mistral by default. Quieter start on macOS.

Fixes found while testing on macOS: the button that copies the prompt and opens the AI service now works there, and the app has its own icon. The environment variable MASCHERA_PORT works as documented, and error details from libraries no longer appear in responses of the local API.

Security update: raised minimum versions of the dependencies (torch, transformers, Flask, Werkzeug, Jinja2, gunicorn), the model is loaded from safetensors only, and training artifacts are no longer shipped. Model and detection are unchanged.
First public release: Linux (AppImage, Flatpak), Windows and Docker.
